title: Era is applied from header.era on replay, but no hunk in this diff ever writes era into the log header
detail: The live side sets state.era and replay reads header.era, yet no hunk adds an era field to any log-header struct nor writes state.era at save time. An era-3 demo's blessed log replays with era 0 (director inactive) and diverges; if the field is absent, the build fails.
recommended_fix: Add era to the log header: extend the header struct, write state.era when saving the log in run_demo, parse it into header.era for replay; re-bless the goldens.

title: color_rgba channel check binds okc but tests !ok — non-integer channel silently accepted as 0
detail: okc is never read; ok is the outer json.Object assertion, always true here. A float/string channel fails the type assertion, yields n=0, and passes the 0..255 range check — malformed data silently defaulting to 0 where the error message itself promises fail-fast on non-ints.
recommended_fix: Change the condition to `if !okc || n < 0 || n > 255 {` so a failed integer assertion is rejected.

title: default_lane is truncated to u8 before the >2 range check — JSON 256..258 wrap into 0..2 and pass
detail: The i32 from jint is cast to u8 before validation: 256/257/258 wrap to 0/1/2 and are silently accepted in both the packet_types and demand-entry loaders. Range validation happens on the truncated value, not the catalog value.
recommended_fix: Validate the i32 before casting, e.g. `dl := jint(...); if dl < 0 || dl > 2 { return ... }; pt.default_lane = u8(dl)`, in both loaders.

title: Set-piece tick fields are cast i32→u64 before any sign check — negative JSON values wrap to ~2^64
evidence:
sp.start_tick = u64(jint(seo, "start_tick", 0))
					sp.duration_ticks = u64(jint(seo, "duration_ticks", 0))
					sp.forecast_lead_ticks = u64(jint(seo, "forecast_lead_ticks", 0))
					if sp.multiplier < 1 || sp.duration_ticks == 0 {
detail: A negative start_tick wraps to a huge u64 (surge never fires); duration_ticks of -1 passes the ==0 check and wraps to ~2^64, making the set-piece window effectively unbounded. The fail-fast validation never sees the sign.
recommended_fix: Range-check the i32 values (start/forecast >= 0, duration >= 1) and fail fast before the u64 casts.

title: Duplicate era in demand.json silently overwrites the earlier Demand_Era — content dropped, arrays leaked
detail: Two eras entries with the same `era` value: the second assignment overwrites the first — its entries/set_pieces dynamic arrays leak and its demand content is silently discarded instead of failing fast on the duplicate.
recommended_fix: Detect that the slot is already populated (or track seen era numbers) and return a Catalog_Error on duplicates.

title: Non-object rows in packet_types/demand arrays are silently skipped via or_continue
evidence:
eo := ev.(json.Object) or_continue
					eeo := ee.(json.Object) or_continue
					seo := se.(json.Object) or_continue
detail: A structurally malformed row (non-object element in entries/eras/set_pieces) is silently dropped by the new 3.1 loaders, while the same diff's comments promise fail-fast on bad catalog data. Bad rows should be load errors, not invisible skips.
recommended_fix: Replace or_continue with an explicit type assertion check that returns a Catalog_Error naming the file and the offending row.

title: load_demo_qos_fixture frees draws/spawns/captures but not demolishes
evidence:
demo, _ := parse_demo(demo_name, string(text_bytes))
	qos := demo.qos_fixture
	delete(demo.draws)
	delete(demo.spawns)
	delete(demo.captures)
	return qos
detail: Demo also owns demolishes ([dynamic]Demolish_Intent, per the Demo struct hunk). Every call for a demo containing demolish intents (drift_check and run_replay paths) leaks that array.
recommended_fix: Add `delete(demo.demolishes)` alongside the other frees before returning.
